values.note: No water, showers or flush toilets from March 15 to April 15 and October 1 to November 30. Boat ramp; the Stockton Lake equestrian trail starts here, with a few non-electric sites by the trailhead where horses can be kept.

note: USACE campground at Hawker Point on Stockton Lake, on a wooded point with two loops on the north and east shores. The shore-side sites of loop A (A03, A07, A09, A11) and of loop B's knob (B02, B04, B05, B06) back onto the open riprap shoreline. --Claude
summary: rec.gov read: 45 sites (A 14 + B 16 electric 30A, B 7 + C 8 non-electric; description says 62), $28/$20 peak, $20/$10 shoulder -> low 10 / high 28 confirmed, Mar 15 - Nov 30 (shoulder months no water), 3-night holiday minimum, 14 nights. Waterfront lead UP: eight shore-side sites earn lakefront. Phone 417-276-7266 to add. PIN is the facility point ~690 m S of the loops: move to 37.6119,-93.7849. Loop C is a separate point 2 km S on its own road (possible split).
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (lakeview -> lakefront): the catalog has no Proximity to Water attribute. Imagery (taken at a low lake level, bare drawdown shore showing): in loop A the sites east of the loop road - A03, A07, A09, A11 (and A13/A14 at the north end) - have their pads ending at the riprapped shoreline, with only bare rock/sand below to the water, ~30-35 m away even at the low level shown; on loop B's knob B02, B04, B05 and B06 end at the riprap the same way, ~25-30 m from the low-water edge. No road, lot, beach or day-use lawn between those pads and the lake, so those eight to ten sites earn lakefront. The loop-B row B14-B20 sits on the loop road with a wooded strip and the road between it and the north shore; the rest are inland across the loop road.
PHONE (to add): rec.gov facility_phone 417-276-7266 ('Call the park (417-276-7266) or project office (417-276-3113) for more information'). None stored.
PIN: stored 37.6064,-93.7811 = the RIDB facility point, on the boat-ramp road ~690 m S of the A/B loops' centre. Move onto the loops: 37.6119,-93.7849 (the loop junction by B10-B14).

CLUSTERS / SPLIT CANDIDATE: loop C (8 non-electric sites C12-C19, 6 reservable; RV 25-30 ft on C13-C16 and C19) is on a separate peninsula at ~37.5922,-93.7790, 2.2 km S of loops A/B, reached by its own branch road leaving the access road ~1.5 km before the A/B loops (imagery shows a row of further short spurs on that road west of the loop, not on recreation.gov). Whether a shared gate controls both is not stated. It meets the 1 km / own-road test; near.py: no other entry within 1 km of loop C. A split would be a small non-electric loop; AWH's call.
SITE COUNT: the description says 62 campsites; the catalog and the availability grid both hold 45 (43 reservable; B02, C12, C13 not reservable). Count written as 45 with the breakdown in sites.note.

RIG LENGTH: every site carries a generic 'Max Vehicle Length 20' attribute, but permitted_equipment gives RV max_length 40-45 ft on all 30 electric sites; max_rig_ft written from the per-equipment lengths (45). 40 of 45 sites take a 23-ft RV.

SEASON / CLOSURE: the calendar shows every site 'Closed' 2026-11-02 through 2026-11-10 and Available again from 11-11 to 11-30 - a short closure not explained in the notices, ending tomorrow; not written as status.
FCFS: the stored note's 'reservable online' is right; no FCFS statement on rec.gov (fcfs not written).

WATER: stored hookups.water true (derived from the note's 'water/electric Apr 16 to Sep 30') left alone: the notice reads 'Drinking water and electric hookups are available during the reservation season, Apr. 16 to Sept. 30', but the catalog carries no Water Hookup attribute on any site - unconfirmed either way.
